RIPARIAN VEGETATION AND WATER QUALITY IN TROPICAL SMALL ISLAND FRESHWATER SYSTEMS: CONSERVATION INSIGHTS FROM BANGKA BELITUNG, INDONESIA

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Henri, Luchman Hakim, Brian Rahardi, Catur Retnaningdyah
Print ISSN : 2523-5664
Online ISSN : 2523-5672

Doi: 10.26480/wcm.01.2026.371.377

ABSTRACT

Freshwater on small tropical islands is scarce and poorly documented. We assessed water quality and riparian habitat condition across the small-island ecosystems of Bangka Belitung, Indonesia, treating them as a coupled system. Forty water samples were collected from 20 freshwater sources on four islands and scored for nine parameters using the National Sanitation Foundation Water Quality Index (NSFWQI). Riparian vegetation was surveyed using nested plots and an adapted Qualitat del Bosc de Ribera (QBR) index. Tinggi, Kelapan, and Pongok Islands were rated Good (WQI 71.20-73.15). Semujur Island was rated Medium (WQI 69.88), held back by acidic water (pH 5.69±0.64) and high TDS (307.03±54.37 mg/L). Riparian quality followed the same pattern: QBR ranged from 45 (Poor) on Semujur to 80 (Good) on Tinggi and tracked water quality closely ( rho = 0.72 p < 0.01 ) WQI also rose with Naturalness ( rho = 0.65 , p < 0.05 ) and dropped as Hemeroby increased ( rho = – 0.68 , p < 0.01 ) so the islands lined up along a gradient from modified Tinggi, just short of semi-natural, to heavily modified Semujur. Principal Component Analysis captured 77.87% of the variance and reproduced the same vegetation-water link. Taken together, the WQI-QBR-Hemeroby combination provides island communities with a practical, low-cost way to track freshwater condition and work toward Sustainable Development Goal 6.
